nodes.name: Co-NTA Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The first step of the procedure was to dissolve 6 mmol of CoCl₂ in 30 mL of deionized water, followed by adding 3 mmol nitrilotriacetic acid under stirring, and then 10 mL isopropanol dropwise. After stirring for a certain period, the solution was poured into the reactor and reacted at 180°C for 6 h. Subsequently, the resultant was centrifugated, washed, and dried to obtain the Co-NTA nanowire product.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of Co-NTA and Co₃O₄: The first step of the procedure was to dissolve 6 mmol of CoCl₂ in 30 mL of deionized water... Subsequently, the resultant was centrifugated, washed, and dried to obtain the Co-NTA nanowire product.

nodes.name: Co3O4 Calcination
nodes.procedure: To obtain the porous rod-like Co₃O₄, Co-NTA was then annealed at 350°C for 4 h.
nodes.source_text: To obtain the porous rod-like Co₃O₄, Co-NTA was then annealed at 350°C for 4 h.

nodes.name: Co3O4/Fe2O3 Hydrothermal Growth
nodes.procedure: A total of 0.1 g Co₃O₄ from above synthesis was dispersed in 35 mL deionized water, where 0.308 g Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, 1.158 g NH₄F, and 2.275 g urea were added under stirring. Then, the solution was poured into the reactor and reacted at 160°C for 12 h. The resultant was then successively centrifugated, washed, dried, and annealed at 350°C for 4 h to obtain the porous nanoheterostructured Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ rods.

The overvoltage of the Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ cathode is 1.08 V... discharge capacity of 14847.8 mAh g⁻¹... can run steadily for 280 cycles... discharge-specific capacity of 12 570.3, 11 376.7, 7520.7, 6477.2, and 5559.9 mAh g⁻¹... pristine Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ cathode exhibits the smallest R_ct of 25.5 Ω... nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows porous rod-like morphology for Co₃O₄ and Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ comprising numerous granular nanoparticles with homogeneous distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) measurements, the Co₃O₄ catalyst possesses a porous rod-like morphology after oxidation of the Co-NTA nanowires in air (Figure 1c), while the Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ compound derived from hydrothermal oxidation treatment maintains the similar rod-like morphology comprising numerous granular nanoparticles with homogeneous distribution.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows uniform distribution of Co, Fe, and O elements throughout the Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ rods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the EDX mapping shows the distribution of the Co, Fe, and O elements in a uniform manner throughout the rods (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals nano-heterostructure with lattice fringes of 0.24 nm (Co₃O₄ (311)) and 0.36 nm (Fe₂O₃ (012)); SAED shows spacings of 0.47, 0.28, and 0.25 nm corresponding to (111), (220), and (110) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image clearly reveals the nano-heterostructure between Co₃O₄ and Fe₂O₃ due to the distinct two sets of lattice fringes within the same region (Figure 1g). Specifically, the spacing of 0.24 nm is attributed to the (311) plane of Co₃O₄ and the spacing of 0.36 nm is the (012) plane of Fe₂O₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms (type IV with hysteresis) show Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface areas of 77.23 m²/g (Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃), 45.24 m²/g (Fe₂O₃), 32.83 m²/g (Co₃O₄); average pore diameters 3.831 nm (Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃), 3.804 nm (Fe₂O₃), 3.403 nm (Co₃O₄).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms in Figure 2a and Figure S3 (Supporting Information) show the adsorption-desorption isotherms of type IV with hysteresis loops and the specific surface area of the Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ catalyst is 77.23 m²g⁻¹, which is higher than that of Fe₂O₃ (45.24 m²g⁻¹) and Co₃O₄ (32.83 m²g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Co 2p peaks at 780.1/794.8 eV (Co₃O₄) shifting to 780.6/795.5 eV (Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃) with Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio increasing from 1.16 to 1.55 indicating more oxygen vacancies and strong interfacial interaction; Fe 2p at ≈713/≈724 eV; O 1s at 529.8, 531.3, 532.6 eV showing increased oxygen vacancies in Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Deconvolution of the main peaks of the Co₃O₄ indicates the Co³⁺ signal at 779 and 794 eV and the Co²⁺ signal at 781 and 795 eV which are slightly shifted by 1.1 and 0.8 eV toward higher bonding energy for the deconvoluted XPS signals of the Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ catalyst... the Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio is calculated to be 1.16 and 1.55 for the Co₃O₄ and Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ catalyst, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman characteristic peaks of Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ shift to higher wavenumbers compared to Co₃O₄, proving existence of oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman tests were conducted on Co₃O₄ and Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ materials. The results show that the characteristic peaks of Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ are shifted to high wavenumbers compared with Co₃O₄ (Figure S4, Supporting Information), proving the existence of oxygen vacancies in the materials.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows pristine Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ cathode has smallest charge transfer resistance R_ct of 25.5 Ω (vs 77.5 Ω for Fe₂O₃, 45.4 Ω for Co₃O₄); after discharge/charge, R_ct changes to 334/59.4 Ω for Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ (vs 666/161 Ω for Fe₂O₃, 594/180 Ω for Co₃O₄).
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the EIS results, the pristine Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ cathode exhibits the smallest R_ct of 25.5Ω, whereas the R_ct for Fe₂O₃ and Co₃O₄ is 77.5 and 45.4Ω, respectively... As for the Co₃O₄/Fe₂O₃ cathode, the R_ct is raised to 334Ω after discharge and drops to 59.4Ω after charge.
